He missed a big and annoying feature of NTSC video: fields.

NTSC was not 60 frames per second. It was 60 fields per second. Each field was 240 lines. The scanner in the camera would pan down and scan 240 lines (the odd numbered lines), then pan back up and scan another 240 lines (the even numbered lines). It would scan down and up 30 times per second (29.97, actually, but close enough).

This looked fine on your CRT television. You wouldn’t notice that you were only seeing 240 lines drawn at a time. The fuzzy projection of the CRT blended them together and the motion still looked smooth.

If you want to scan that format digitally and store it in 720 × 480 frames you’re going to see the two interlaced fields whenever something is moving in the frame. There are various techniques for deinterlacing NTSC video, but often it’s done poorly and either way you don’t have true 480 line frames.
